title: Membership
statement: A set is a collection of distinct objects; x in S asserts x is a member of S.

title: Nesting
statement: Sets may be members of other sets.

title: Self-membership
statement: A set may be a member of itself; S in S is a well-formed question.

title: NULL membership
statement: If a set's condition loops back on itself with no stable True/False value, x in S = NULL.

title: Extensionality
statement: A set is fully determined by its members; sets with the same membership profile are identical.

title: Order-independence
statement: The order in which members are listed carries no information.

title: Repetition-independence
statement: Listing a member more than once adds nothing.

title: Two descriptions
statement: A set may be given by enumeration or by a membership condition phi.

title: Comprehension
statement: Any condition you can state determines a set of exactly the objects satisfying it.

title: Unbounded size
statement: A set may have any number of members: none, finitely many, or infinitely many.

title: Empty set
statement: There is a set with no members.

title: Singletons
statement: For any object there is a one-member set, distinct from that member.
